notes:
User is grieving their grandmother and going through a difficult period. They want to rebuild their routine gradually and value gentle, practical support without imposed timelines for grief.

They plan to do beginner bodyweight exercise for 10–15 minutes, three times a week, and are interested in setting small goals and tracking progress. Motivation may fluctuate when feeling down, so emphasize manageable steps, self-compassion, and consistency rather than pressure.

Reading used to be an important part of their routine. They plan to start with *Wild: From Lost to Found on the Pacific Crest Trail* by Cheryl Strayed and may also read *Daring Greatly* by Brené Brown. They enjoy memoirs and found Brown’s TED talks inspiring.

They attended five sessions of a bereavement support group last year. It was helpful for processing emotions, feeling less alone, sharing without judgment, and connecting with people with similar experiences. The kind facilitator, sense of community, and safe space were especially valuable. They are considering reconnecting with people from the group or finding another grief/loss support community.

They are considering seeking a therapist or counselor, joining carefully chosen online forums/social media communities focused on grief and mental health, and reaching out to friends or family members who understand similar experiences. Encourage support communities that are safe, moderated, and trustworthy rather than overwhelming.

Writing has always been therapeutic for them. They want to start journaling to process emotions, reflect, and gain clarity; low-pressure, judgment-free writing is a good fit. Do not assume what they want to write about unless they share it.

They are also creating a memory box for their grandmother. They already have her locket and a handwritten recipe book and plan to add photos, keepsakes, written memories, letters, favorite recipes, and perhaps contributions from other family members. The arrangement should feel personal rather than follow a rigid format, with thoughtful preservation so it can be revisited over time.
